evidence: Clear directory-based modularity with 5 top-level packages (data, models, networks, options, utils) and shallow depth (max 2)
Each module has cohesive responsibilities (e.g., data loading, model definitions, network architectures, options parsing, utilities)
No inter-service communication patterns (e.g., no REST/gRPC clients, message queues, or service discovery)
Centralized entry points (train.py, test.py) that orchestrate modules without being decoupled via interfaces or adapters
Shared dependencies across modules (e.g., utils used by data, models, and networks); no strict dependency inversion
Low fan-out (avg 3.35) suggests internal cohesion and limited external coupling, typical of monolithic modules
No evidence of ports/adapters (e.g., no explicit interfaces for infrastructure concerns like DB, APIs, or external services)
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., train.py directly imports from multiple modules) may hinder testability and maintainability
Lack of explicit architectural boundaries (e.g., no hexagonal ports) makes it harder to swap infrastructure components
Monolithic deployment model limits scalability and independent evolution of components
